purpose: Specify the time resolution of ICP estimates — how quickly can the system detect a clinically meaningful ICP change?

specification.time_resolution_target_sec: 60 (1-minute resolution is sufficient for clinical decisions; faster is better but not required)
specification.rationale: ICP changes that require urgent intervention (e.g., acute herniation) develop over minutes-to-hours, not seconds. 60-sec resolution captures all clinically meaningful dynamics.
constraint_chain: Transport delay: 10-180 min (slowest stage — dominates time resolution)
Clearance: 30-180 min (limits how quickly concentration reflects new release rate)
specification.bottleneck: Transport + clearance. The system CANNOT be faster than the molecule's journey from brain to sensor. This is a PHYSICAL LIMIT, not an engineering one.
specification.implication: P-09 is NOT a real-time monitor for acute events (e.g., seizure, acute herniation). It is a TREND monitor for chronic ICP management (similar to CGM for chronic glucose management).

clinical_use_case_clarification: P-09 is suited for: (a) chronic hydrocephalus management (adjustable shunt tuning over days-weeks), (b) post-operative monitoring (trends over hours-days), (c) home monitoring (daily ICP trends). NOT suited for: (a) acute trauma monitoring (need real-time, invasive catheter remains gold standard), (b) intraoperative monitoring (need real-time).
